name: The Resort at Paws Up
positioning: All-inclusive luxury ranch resort on a working cattle ranch in Montana, with private homes and seasonal riverside glamping camps along the Blackfoot River
best_for: Travelers who want horseback riding, fly fishing and ranch activities on a vast wilderness property
Families and groups wanting a private multi-bedroom home or an entire glamping camp to themselves

facts.text: The resort covers 37,000 acres of wilderness, with over 100 miles of trails and 10 miles of the Blackfoot River.
Paws Up is a working cattle ranch.
Stays include gourmet meals, airport transfers, on-property transportation and access to resort amenities.
Paws Up is a gratuity-free resort.
The six glamping camps sit along the Blackfoot River or on scenic bluffs.
Glamping tents have king-size feather beds, ensuite bathrooms with rain showers and heated floors, and private decks.
The Historic Homes are the original historic homes of the Paws Up ranch land.
Wilderness Estates have a lofted game room, a private hot tub and a living room centered on a large stone-and-timber fireplace.
Luxury home guests get a Lexus SUV for personal use at the ranch.
Paws Up sits within the 'golden triangle' of Western trout fly fishing, with access to the Blackfoot and Clearwater rivers.
Ranch activities include cattle drives, river rafting, Montana line dancing, lasso lessons and hatchet throwing.
Dining has seven options, from fine dining to rustic chuck wagon dinners.

highlights.text: Spa Town's private treatment tents have heated massage tables and open-air views of a meadow often spotted with horses.
Every glamping camp has its own Dining Pavilion, a dedicated chef and a Camp Butler.
The all-day Frontiersman Ride is led by equestrian in chief Jackie Kecskes or her head wrangler.
In spring 2018, Paws Up brought home five rescued mustangs through the Bureau of Land Management's Wild Horse and Burro Program.
A complimentary pet massage comes with any 60-minute spa service.

considerations.text: Glamping is open only seasonally, from mid-May through mid-October.
Only select homes are pet-friendly, for dogs only; pets are not permitted in the glamping accommodations.
WhataHotel notes the remote wilderness location requires significant travel time.
